placements.why: No existing strata category covers instrument calibration/verification as an organizational practice; this envelope's content (a calibration state verified against reference plates) names a genuinely new organizational-strategy category, not a leaf-grain subject.
placements.title: Instrument Calibration and Verification Practice
placements.frame: What calibration procedures and verification standards does the organization treat as authoritative for its instruments?

placements.title: Calibration claims gain authority through verification against reference standards
placements.frame: What reference standard or verification procedure is invoked to substantiate an instrument's calibration state?
placements.why: The lead astronomer's calibration assertion and the record's restatement of instrument and calibration fields both point to the same recurring theme: an instrument's calibrated state is established as trustworthy by verifying it against a named reference standard. This is a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding, not a one-time fact — the specific 88.4 MHz/June-plates measurement is evidence for it, not the leaf itself. No existing leaf in the (currently empty) graph structure covers this theme, so it is minted fresh under the newly minted Calibration stratum.
